title: A tiny test framework
description:
Write the smallest useful test framework: register tests, run them, report.

```
[ ok ] addition
[FAIL] parse empty: expected 0, got -1 (test.cpp:21)
[ ok ] parse number
2 of 3 passed
```
hints: `#define TEST(name) static void name(); static bool name##_reg{(registry().push_back({#name, name}), true)}; static void name()` (lesson 17.01).
A global "current test failed" flag set by `CHECK_EQ` and read after each test runs is enough.
requirements: `TEST(name)` registers a function; `CHECK_EQ(a, b)` records a failure with the values and line.
One failing check does not stop the other tests.
The program returns non-zero when anything failed, so a build can stop.
stretch: Run only tests whose name contains a word passed on the command line.
